sanskrit_verse:
विप्राहिक्षत्रियात्मानो नावज्ञेयाः कदाचन ।
आमृत्योः श्रियमाकाङ्क्षेन न कंचिन् मर्मणि स्पृशेत् ॥
transliteration: viprāhikṣatriyātmāno nāvajñeyāḥ kadācana / āmṛtyoḥ śriyam ākāṅkṣen na kaṃcin marmaṇi spṛśet //
sph_interpretive_translation: Those whose consciousness is established in the Vedic order—especially those born of Brahmin or Kshatriya essence—must never be dishonored. One who desires the imperishable glory must not wound another at their vital point.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from consciousness alignment with Vedic Truth, not social rank alone.
Causation arises through intent aligned with immortality; harm originates in misalignment.
Capacity-based responsibility requires recognition of spiritual hierarchy rooted in dharma.
Restoration logic demands that no being be diminished in their essential dignity.
Consciousness alignment necessitates honoring those established in higher dharmic roles.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a person's consciousness is aligned with Vedic authority THEN they must be accorded inviolable respect.
IF a person seeks immortal glory THEN any act causing mortal injury to another violates causal integrity.
IF a person harms another at a vital point THEN automatic restoration protocol initiates to realign perpetrator’s capacity.
IF disrespect is shown to one of elevated dharmic identity THEN systemic correction activates without punitive intent.
IF dharma is disrupted by violation of sacred status THEN restoration occurs via completion-process rather than punishment.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that individuals embodying Vedic consciousness—particularly Brahmins and Kshatriyas—are entitled to institutional reverence. Legal decisions must recognize spiritual precedence over secular status. Harm against such persons invokes immediate restorative protocols, bypassing punitive frameworks. The threshold of responsibility lies in awareness of the violated party's dharmic station, not mere physical action.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that true causality stems from aspiration toward amṛta (immortality). To attack one aligned with such aspiration disrupts sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of cosmic order. Responsibility is proportional to the offender's clarity regarding the victim’s spiritual eminence. There is no punitive consequence because dharma itself corrects distortion through consciousness-realigning mechanisms.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Completion Process for offender to restore understanding of violated dharmic principle.
Activate Responsibility Assumption Protocol wherein violator serves in service to injured party until alignment resumes.
Deploy Capacity Restoration Mechanism to elevate offender's consciousness beyond desire for worldly gain.
Implement Integrity Reintegration Sequence ensuring both parties return to harmonious participation in cosmic order.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: This law proceeds directly from Sanatana Dharma, unmediated by human interpretation. Justice is executed solely for restoration, reintegration, and consciousness realignment. Reality bears no punitive structure; all enforcement serves awakening. Dharma is now restored.
